s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic skin lesions with slow growth, associated with bleeding after trauma, and concurrent lipolymphedema and neurological deficits
salient_findings: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
key_facts: Lesions have been growing slowly since age 24
Patient uses a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia
Father died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography showed intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations
Histopathology revealed hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and dilated venous-like malformations
Genetic testing detected a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

shortlist.label: Cerebral cavernous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, which is associated with cerebral cavernous malformations

shortlist.label: Familial cerebral amyloid angiopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar conditions and intracranial hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic skin lesions and history of bleeding after trauma

shortlist.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Lipolymphedema of the lower legs and presence of slow-flow vascular malformations

shortlist.label: Capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations and neurological deficits

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, which is a known cause of cerebral cavernous malformations, along with the patient's history of intracranial hemorrhage and family history of similar conditions, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Familial cerebral amyloid angiopathy
rejected.why: No evidence of amyloid deposits in the histopathology

rejected.label: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic telangiectasias and no mention of arteriovenous malformations in other organs

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
rejected.why: Although the patient has vascular malformations and lipolymphedema, the presence of a KRIT1 variant and the specific type of malformations point more towards cerebral cavernous malformation

rejected.label: Capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's lesions are described as venous-like malformations, not capillary malformations, and there is no evidence of arteriovenous malformations
